info.desc: Exit Planet Dust is the debut album by British electronica duo The Chemical Brothers, released in the UK on June 26, 1995 and the US on August 15 1995 (see 1995 in music). The title is a reference to their departure from their earlier name "The Dust Brothers". In 2004, the album was packaged with 1997s Dig Your Own Hole in a limited edition box set as part of EMI's "2CD Originals" collection. It was certified platinum by the BPI on January 1, 1996. .
info.engineers: Steve Dub, Tim Holmes / Mike Marsh

podcast.body: Released in 1995, this album is considered the "year zero" of Big Beat. Its founders, Tom Rowlands and Ed Simons, originally called themselves Dust Brothers but had to change their name due to a lawsuit threat from another American band with the same name. While preserving elements of acid house and nocturnal club music, the album was well-received by critics as a "new breath of fresh air" and achieved unexpected commercial success. "El disco se llama Silla que Tom Roblanz y Ed Siamonds, sus fundadores, se hacían llamar Dust Brothers, pero tuvieron que cambiar lo debido a que otra banda americana que se llamaba igual, había amenazado con demandarles."

podcast.body: The Chemical Brothers released their first album, *Exit Planet Dust*, in 1995. By this time, they had already become a recognized entity within British rock music, having befriended many prominent figures and being played in numerous non-electronic bars. Despite initial rejection from both the hardcore rave and rock communities, the album was a resounding success, quickly establishing their sound. Its release served as the official launchpad for the Big Beat culture, inspiring many other UK DJs, including Fatboy Slim, Groove Armada, and The Crystal Method, to transition into producing their own studio albums. "El éxito forrotundo, curiosamente al que al principio tenían el rechazo un poco de esos dos mundos, con ese disco muy rápido se asentaron."
